header.title: Grid
header.description: Declarative layout on top of CSS Grid, made of three pieces. `Grid` defines the columns (`columns`, `template` or `auto`). `Row` is a fixed 12-column Grid. `Col` sets how many columns each child spans, with mobile-first values per breakpoint. To limit the page width, pair it with `Container`.

playground.title: Playground
playground.description: Tweak the props and see the result and the code instantly. With `auto`, `columns` is ignored and each column is at least 10rem wide. With `align`, the first cell is taller so the alignment is visible.

tracks.title: How columns are defined
tracks.description: Grid builds `grid-template-columns` in one of three ways. If you pass more than one, `auto` wins, then `template`, and `columns` last.

items.columns: Equal columns. It is the default mode (12). From 2 to 4 columns they stack on mobile unless you change `stack`.
items.template: Columns with different widths, like a fixed sidebar and flexible content. Accepts any CSS value.
items.auto: Cards that rearrange themselves based on the available space, without breakpoints. The minimum width comes from `minItemWidth`.

base.title: Base
base.description: `columns` splits the width into equal columns and children are placed in order, moving to the next row when one is full. The examples use this cell and these demo styles.

stack.title: Stacking on mobile
stack.description: With 2 to 4 equal columns, Grid switches to a single column below 640px (`stack="sm"` by default). `stack="md"` stacks below 768px and `stack={false}` always keeps the columns. Resize the window to see the difference.

rowCol.title: Row and Col (12 columns)
rowCol.description: `Row` is a 12-column Grid that never stacks. Each `Col` spans `span` columns (12 by default). When the sum goes over 12, the next Col wraps to a new row; you don't need one Row per line.

responsive.title: Responsive
responsive.description: Spans are mobile-first: `span` applies from 0 and each breakpoint (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`) replaces it from its minimum width up. If you skip a breakpoint, it inherits the previous one. The example shows 1 column on mobile, 2 from 768px and 3 from 1024px. Breakpoints depend on the window width, not the container.

gap.title: Spacing
gap.description: `gap` accepts a spacing token (`4` is `var(--gem-space-4)`), any other number (treated as pixels) or any CSS length. `rowGap` and `columnGap` split vertical and horizontal spacing. Without `gap`, it uses `--gem-grid-gutter` (1rem), which becomes `--gem-grid-gutter-lg` (1.5rem) from 1024px.

auto.title: Automatic columns
auto.description: `auto` creates as many columns as fit, each at least `minItemWidth` wide (16rem by default). With few items, `fit` stretches them to fill the row and `fill` keeps empty slots and each cell's width. It doesn't need `stack`: on narrow screens it ends up with a single column.

template.title: Custom template
template.description: `template` takes the `grid-template-columns` value as is. Use `minmax(0, …)` so long content doesn't overflow the column. Templates don't stack on their own; pass `stack` if you want a single column on mobile.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: `offset` leaves that many columns empty before the Col; in practice it starts at column offset + 1. It has per-breakpoint variants (`offsetSm`, `offsetMd`…) and `0` restores automatic placement.

align.title: Alignment
align.description: `align` on Grid or Row vertically aligns every cell in the row (`align-items`). `align` on Col aligns only that cell (`align-self`). `justify` distributes leftover space when the columns don't fill the width, for example with a fixed-width template.

nested.title: Nested grids
nested.description: A Col can hold its own Grid. The inner Grid builds its columns on that Col's width, not the page's.

pageLayout.title: Page layout
pageLayout.description: Row and Col build the overall structure: full-width header and footer, and a sidebar that moves to the side from 768px. Inside the main content, a Grid with `auto="fit"` arranges the cards without breakpoints. On a real page, wrap it in a `Container` to limit the width.

header.title: Grid API
header.description: API reference for the Grid, Row and Col React components: props, CSS classes, CSS variables, tokens and exported types.

demos.title: Demos
demos.description: For examples and usage details, visit the component demos page.

import.title: Import
import.description: Import them from the main entry or from their subpath to load only the layout.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body: Grid, Row and Col accept HTML attributes (HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>) and pass them to the root element. ref reaches the element. Layout props become CSS variables inside style (for example --gem-grid-cols or --gem-col-span), merged with the style you pass.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.order: Visual order follows the DOM. Avoid reordering with CSS: screen readers and keyboard focus follow the source order.
a11y.landmark: With as you can render main, aside, nav, header or footer instead of a <div>.
a11y.list: For a list of cards, use as="ul" on Grid and as="li" on each child so the number of items is announced.
a11y.label: If there are several nav, aside or section elements, name them with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

cssClasses.title: CSS classes
cssClasses.description: Classes you can use to override styles.

rules.root: Grid and Row root element. Receives `className` and `classNames.root`.
rules.cols: Applied with `columns` when there is no `template` or `auto`.
rules.align: Applied with `align` on Grid or Row (`align-items`).
rules.justify: Applied with `justify` on Grid or Row (`justify-content`).
rules.row: Added on Row, on top of `.gem-grid`.
rules.colSpan: Applied from `span`. On a Col it only sets `--gem-col-span`; on elements without `.gem-col` it also places the column, so you can use it on plain markup.

cssVariables.title: CSS variables
cssVariables.description: Set in the root element's `style`. The ones written inline can only be redefined with `!important` (for example, the site's Tailwind utilities); `--gem-grid-gap` can be changed from a class if you don't pass `gap`.

items.--gem-grid-cols: Number of equal columns. Set by `columns`.
items.--gem-grid-gap: Space between cells. Set by `gap`; without `gap`, it uses the theme gutter.
items.--gem-grid-min: Minimum column width with `auto`. Set by `minItemWidth`.
items.--gem-col-span: Columns the Col spans from 0. Set by `span`.
items.--gem-col-{bp}-start: Starting column from each breakpoint. Set by `offsetSm`…`offsetXxl`.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: gem-system tokens used by the grid. Redefine them globally to change every grid.

items.--gem-space-{n}: Spacing scale used by `gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap` when they receive a token.

types.title: Exported types
types.description: Available from @gem-org/gem-system to type your own wrappers. The file also includes the Flex types.

props.title: Props
props.description: All three components also accept the root element's HTML attributes.

items.columns: Number of equal columns. Ignored with `template` or `auto`.
items.auto: Creates automatic columns with `repeat(auto-fit | auto-fill, …)`. Use it with `minItemWidth`.
items.minItemWidth: Minimum column width with `auto`. A number is pixels.
items.stack: Breakpoint below which it stacks into one column. Defaults to `"sm"` with 2 to 4 equal columns and `false` otherwise.
items.gap: Space between cells: spacing token, pixels or CSS length.
items.justify: Column distribution when there is leftover space (`justify-content`). `stretch` uses `justify-items`.
items.className: Extra classes for the root element.
items.classNames: Per-slot classes. `root` is added to the root element.
items.style: Inline styles. Merged with the grid CSS variables.

items.stack: Stacks into one column below the breakpoint. Doesn't stack by default.
items.gap: Space between Cols: spacing token, pixels or CSS length.
items.justify: Column distribution when there is leftover space (`justify-content`).
items.classNames: Per-slot classes. `root` is added to the root element.
items.style: Inline styles. Merged with the grid CSS variables.

col.title: Col
col.description: Cell that spans a number of columns of a Row or a 12-column Grid.

items.offset: Empty columns before the Col. `0` restores automatic placement.
items.className: Extra classes for the root element.
items.classNames: Per-slot classes. `root` is added to the root element.
items.style: Inline styles. Merged with the Col CSS variables.
